newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle market quiet, no trade - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle market quiet, no trade - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Monday were quiet, with no sales reported following moderately active trade last week at top prices mostly of $64.00 per cwt, several feedlot sources said.
A few packer bids were reported Monday at $63.00, but those were passed by owners asking $65.00, sources said.
Owners priced cattle at $65.00 amid ideas packers had only enough cattle to get them through midweek, sources said.
Fed cattle prices also were seen underpinned by talk most feedlots were current in their marketings.
Support in fed cattle prices this week could be shaken if beef demand falls dramatically as some expect following active sales the past few weeks, market sources said.

Beef sales have been strong as retailers stocked up for end-of-month promotions and for Independence Day features. But most retailers were finished booking for the holiday and purchases this week would be restocking for fill-in purposes, some sources noted.

The Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma cattle showlist was pegged near 89,000 head, up 7,500 from last week and Kansas was estimated near 92,000, steady with last week. Nebraska's showlist was estimated near 85,000 head, about the same as last week.
